Let \(\lambda=2\pi n\). For fixed \(x\in[-1,1]\), the vertical cross-section of \(\Omega\) has length
\[
2(1-x^4)^{1/4},
\]
so
\[
I_n=\int_{-1}^{1}2(1-x^4)^{1/4}\cos(\lambda x)\,dx.
\]

Only the endpoints \(x=\pm1\) contribute to the algebraic asymptotics. Near \(x=1\), putting \(t=1-x\),
\[
2(1-x^4)^{1/4}
=2(4t-6t^2+4t^3-t^4)^{1/4}
=2\sqrt2\,t^{1/4}\left(1-\frac38t+O(t^2)\right).
\]
The same expansion holds near \(x=-1\). Thus the endpoint coefficients are
\[
A=2\sqrt2,\qquad B=-\frac{3\sqrt2}{4}.
\]

Using
\[
\int_0^\infty t^\alpha \cos(\lambda-\lambda t)\,dt
=\Gamma(\alpha+1)\lambda^{-\alpha-1}
\cos\!\left(\lambda-\frac{\pi(\alpha+1)}2\right),
\]
and \(\lambda=2\pi n\), so \(\cos\lambda=1,\sin\lambda=0\), the two endpoints together give
\[
I_n=
2A\Gamma\!\left(\frac54\right)\lambda^{-5/4}\cos\frac{5\pi}{8}
+
2B\Gamma\!\left(\frac94\right)\lambda^{-9/4}\cos\frac{9\pi}{8}
+O(\lambda^{-13/4}).
\]
Now
\[
2A\Gamma\!\left(\frac54\right)\cos\frac{5\pi}{8}
=
-\frac{\sqrt{4-2\sqrt2}\,\Gamma(1/4)}{2},
\]
which matches and cancels the given correction term.

For the next coefficient,
\[
2B\Gamma\!\left(\frac94\right)\cos\frac{9\pi}{8}
=
2\left(-\frac{3\sqrt2}{4}\right)
\left(\frac{5}{16}\Gamma\!\left(\frac14\right)\right)
\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}}2\right)
=
\frac{15\sqrt{4+2\sqrt2}}{64}\Gamma\!\left(\frac14\right).
\]
Therefore
\[
I_n+
\frac{\sqrt{4-2\sqrt2}\,\Gamma(1/4)}
{2(2\pi)^{5/4}n^{5/4}}
=
\frac{15\sqrt{4+2\sqrt2}\,\Gamma(1/4)}
{64(2\pi)^{9/4}n^{9/4}}
+o(n^{-9/4}).
\]

Hence the required limit is
\[
\boxed{\frac{15\sqrt{4+2\sqrt2}\,\Gamma(1/4)}{64(2\pi)^{9/4}}}.
\]
